requirements.title: The health command after a landing
requirements.rationale: A change that passed its gate and its review can still break the main branch once it sits on top of everything else; only a run on the landed commit shows it.

criteria.condition: the scheduler calls the step of an item in `verifying` whose workspace is `green` and which belongs to no incident
criteria.action: read the item's change (`change.Service.Get` of package 05 for its number, the hub client's `Change` for its `landed.sha`), run the workspace's health command on a clone of the workspace at the landed commit through `workspace.Service.RunHealth` with a tail of 200 lines, and, when the command exits 0 within the workspace's health timeout, append the entry `health` with the text `health command passed on <commit>` to the item's thread and move the item to `publishing`
criteria.contract: `RunHealth` was called once, with the workspace's slug, the change's `landed.sha` and 200; the item is `publishing`; the workspace is still `green`; no incident is stored; no notification was sent

setup: a health service over a copy of the store template with the real item service and inbox, the fake hub holding change 7 of item 12 landed as commit C, a stub of package 05's `change.Service.Get` answering `Record{Workspace: 'demo', Change: 7}` for item 12, and a stub in place of `workspace.Service` that records `RunHealth` and `SetState`
check.pseudocode: new file internal/health/verify_test.go, fixtures in internal/health/helpers_test.go: stub.RunHealth returns {ExitCode: 0}; err = svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12); assert err == nil; assert stub.healthCalls == [('demo', C, 200)]; assert items.Get(12).State == 'publishing'; assert the thread's entries hold {kind: 'health', text: 'health command passed on ' + C}; assert stub.state('demo') == 'green'; assert svc.Incident('demo') is none; assert notifier.events is empty

criteria.condition: the health command run on an item's landed commit exits with a code other than 0, or does not end within the workspace's health timeout
criteria.action: set the workspace's state to `red` with `workspace.Service.SetState`, store an incident for the item in the phase `repairing` with the commit and the last 200 lines of the command's output, append the entry `health_failed` to the item's thread, call `Notify` of `internal/notify` with the event `workspace_red`, and leave the item `verifying`
criteria.contract: the workspace's state is `red`; the item is still `verifying`; the incident holds the landed commit and at most 200 lines of output; the entry's text is `health command exited <N> on <commit>` or `health command timed out on <commit>`; exactly one notification was sent for the incident, with `event: workspace_red`, the workspace, the item's number and the item thread's URL path

setup: the fixtures of the passing case, with a recording notifier
check.pseudocode: in internal/health/verify_test.go, a table over stub results {ExitCode 3 with 250 lines of tail -> entry 'health command exited 3 on C', TimedOut -> 'health command timed out on C'}: svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12); assert stub.state('demo') == 'red'; assert items.Get(12).State == 'verifying'; inc = svc.Incident('demo'); assert inc.Phase == 'repairing' and inc.Item == 12 and inc.Commit == C and len(inc.Output) <= 200; assert the entry text; assert notifier.events == [{Event: 'workspace_red', Workspace: 'demo', Item: 12, Thread: the item thread's path}]; call VerifyStep again; assert still one notification and one health_failed entry

criteria.condition: the item's change cannot be read (package 05 holds no record, the hub does not answer), the change is not landed, or `RunHealth` returns an error instead of a result (the clone failed, the hub is not available, the command could not be started)
criteria.action: decide nothing about the workspace and return the error from the step, so that the scheduler calls the step again
criteria.contract: the step returns a non-nil error that names the cause; the workspace's state, the item's state and the item's thread are as before the call; no incident is stored and no notification is sent

check.pseudocode: in internal/health/verify_test.go, a table over {the fake hub answers the change read 502, the change's state is 'open' with landed null, stub.RunHealth returns an error 'cannot clone demo: …'}: err = svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12); assert err != nil; assert stub.setStateCalls is empty; assert items.Get(12).State == 'verifying'; assert the thread has no entry of this package; assert svc.Incident('demo') is none; assert notifier.events is empty; then with the cause removed assert VerifyStep moves the item to 'publishing'

criteria.condition: a workspace is `red` and an item of it that is `verifying` is neither the item nor the repair item of the workspace's open incident
criteria.action: run no health command for that item and leave it `verifying`, and, at the first call of its step after the workspace is `green` again, run its health command on the head of the default branch (`head_sha` of the hub's workspace object) instead of its own landed commit
criteria.contract: no call of `RunHealth` for the item while the workspace is `red`; the first call afterwards carries the hub's `head_sha`; a result of that run is handled as REQ-1.1 and REQ-1.2 say, with that commit

setup: items 12 and 13 of 'demo' both `verifying`; an open incident of item 12; the fake hub's `head_sha` of 'demo' is H, item 13's landed commit is D
check.pseudocode: in internal/health/verify_test.go: svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item13) three times; assert no RunHealth call for D or H and items.Get(13).State == 'verifying'; close the incident as REQ-2.3 does (workspace green); stub.RunHealth returns {ExitCode: 0}; svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item13); assert the last health call == ('demo', H, 200); assert items.Get(13).State == 'publishing'

criteria.action: for any incident, keep in the store its phase, the output of each failed health command, every commit a health command ran on with its result, the number of its repair item and the numbers of the reverting changes it opened, and continue the incident from that record when the step of its item or of its repair item is called after a pause or after a restart of nightshiftd, creating no second repair item and asking the hub for no second revert of a change

the incident of item 12 stored in the phase `reverting` with the repair item 13, whose change 9 is reverted by change 10, which has landed
check.pseudocode: new file internal/health/revert_test.go: reopen the store; svc2.VerifyStep(ctx, item12); assert items.List('demo') holds no item beside 12 and its repair item 13; assert the fake hub saw no POST …/changes/9/revert; assert it saw exactly one POST …/changes/7/revert; assert svc2.Incident('demo').Phase == 'reverting' and its output and commits tried equal those stored before the restart

requirements.title: Fix forward: one repair
requirements.rationale: Most breakages are small, and a fix on top keeps the work that landed; one attempt bounds what a broken main branch may cost.

criteria.condition: an incident of an item is in the phase `repairing` and has no repair item
criteria.action: create one repair item with the item service's `CreateLinked(ctx, <the item>, 'defect', <text>)`, the text naming the landed change and the commit; give it the package of the item it repairs with `(*impl.Service).UsePackageOf` (new in package 06's `internal/impl`, added by this package); ask for its sessions in the repair class with `SetClass(ctx, repair, sched.ClassRepair)`; mark it with `land.Service.SetRepair(ctx, repair, true)`; hand it one finding of the source `health` whose `Output` is the last 200 lines of the health command's output with `Rework`; move it from `new` to `ready`; and append once the entry `repair` with the text `workspace <slug> is red; repair started for change <n>` to the thread of the item whose landing failed, marking it unread
criteria.contract: the incident stores the repair item's number before anything else is asked of it; the repair item is `ready`, a child of the item, of the kind `defect`; `Rework` received exactly one finding `{Source: 'health', Text: 'health command failed on <commit> after change <ref> landed', Output: <the tail>}`; a later call of the step for the same incident creates no second item, and repeats only the calls the record does not show as done; the thread holds exactly one `repair` entry and it is marked unread; the hub saw no revert request

setup: the fixtures of REQ-1.2 with recording stubs of package 06's `Rework`, `SetClass` and `UsePackageOf` and of package 07's `SetRepair`
check.pseudocode: new file internal/health/repair_test.go: svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12) with the failing health stub; inc = svc.Incident('demo'); r = inc.Repair; assert items.Get(r).State == 'ready' and its parent == 12 and its kind == 'defect'; assert impl.calls == [UsePackageOf(r, 12), SetClass(r, sched.ClassRepair), Rework(r, [{Source: 'health', Text: 'health command failed on ' + C + ' after change demo#7 landed', Output: the tail}])]; assert lander.calls == [SetRepair(r, true)]; make impl.Rework fail once in a second run of the case: the first step returns the error, the second calls Rework again and creates no second item; assert count(entries of kind 'repair' in item 12's thread) == 1 and the thread is unread; assert the fake hub saw no revert request

criteria.condition: the scheduler calls the step of a repair item in `verifying`, which packages 06 and 07 implemented, gated, reviewed and landed as any item although the workspace is `red`
criteria.action: read the commit the repair item's change landed as, run the health command on it through `RunHealth` with a tail of 200 lines, and add the commit and its result to the incident's commits tried
criteria.contract: `RunHealth` is called with the slug, the `landed.sha` of the repair item's change and 200; the workspace is `red` until the result is handled; a call of the step of the item whose landing failed, while the repair item is not yet `verifying` and waits on no decision, changes nothing and returns nil

check.pseudocode: in internal/health/repair_test.go: walk the repair item r to 'verifying' with its change 9 landed as R on the fake hub; svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12) first: assert nil, no health call, nothing changed; stub.RunHealth for R returns {ExitCode: 0}; svc.VerifyStep(ctx, r); assert the health call == ('demo', R, 200); assert stub.setStateCalls == ['red', 'green']; assert items.Get(12).State == 'publishing' and items.Get(r).State == 'publishing'; assert lander.calls ends with SetRepair(r, false); assert svc.Incident('demo') is none; assert item 12's thread holds 'health command passed on ' + R and 'workspace demo is green again'; assert the fake hub saw no revert request

criteria.condition: the health command exits 0 within the health timeout on the commit a repair item's change landed as
criteria.action: set the workspace's state to `green`, close the incident, remove the repair mark with `SetRepair(ctx, repair, false)`, append the entries `health` and `workspace_green` to the thread of the item whose landing failed, and move that item and the repair item to `publishing`
criteria.contract: the workspace's state is `green`; both items are `publishing`; the incident's phase is `closed`; the hub saw no revert request; the `workspace_green` entry's text is `workspace <slug> is green again`

criteria.condition: the repair item of an incident in the phase `repairing` waits on a decision of a kind other than `approval` (`session_failed`, `review_disagreement`, `session_limit`, `blocked` or `conflict`), or is `abandoned`
criteria.action: end the repair: close that decision with the inbox's `Close` and the reason `repair ended; the landing is reverted`, abandon the repair item with the item service's `Abandon` where it is not abandoned already, and go on to the revert of REQ-3.1 with the decision's kind as the reason
criteria.contract: the repair item is `abandoned` and has no open decision; no second repair item is created; the incident's phase is `reverting` with the reason `session failed twice` for `session_failed`, `review disagreement` for `review_disagreement`, and `repair stopped: <kind>` or `repair abandoned` otherwise; a repair item that waits on an `approval` decision is left alone and the incident stays `repairing`

setup: the decision kinds of packages 04, 06 and 07 declared in the test's inbox by name, with one option each
check.pseudocode: in internal/health/repair_test.go, a table over the repair item r {in 'implementing' with an open session_failed decision -> reason 'session failed twice'; in 'reviewing' with review_disagreement -> 'review disagreement'; in 'implementing' with blocked -> 'repair stopped: blocked'; abandoned by the person -> 'repair abandoned'; in 'landing' with an open approval decision -> untouched}: svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12); for the first four assert inbox.OpenDecisions(r) is empty, the closed decision's reason == 'repair ended; the landing is reverted', items.Get(r).State == 'abandoned', inc.Phase == 'reverting' and inc.Reason; for the last assert the decision is still open, r is 'landing' and inc.Phase == 'repairing'

requirements.title: Revert, and a main branch that stays unhealthy
requirements.rationale: A repair that did not help must not be followed by another: taking the landing back is the one step that is known to have been healthy before.

criteria.condition: a repair ended as REQ-2.4 says, or the health command exits with a code other than 0 or times out on the commit the repair item's change landed as
criteria.action: move the incident to the phase `reverting`, append once the entry `revert` to the thread of the item whose landing failed, marking it unread, and ask the hub with `POST …/changes/{number}/revert` to revert the repair item's change where it landed, and the item's change once the repair's reverting change has landed or where the repair's change did not land
criteria.contract: the entry's text is `repair did not help (<reason>); reverting change <n>`, with ` and change <m>` for a landed repair, the reason one of those of REQ-2.4, `health command exited <N>` or `health command timed out`; a repair's change that did not land is not reverted; the revert of the item's change is not asked before the land of the repair's reverting change was answered `landed`; an answer `409 already_reverted` is taken as the change `error.details.reverted_by` names and no second revert is asked

setup: the fake hub extended with the revert route: a landed change gets a reverting change with `reverts` set, a second request answers 409 already_reverted with `reverted_by`
a recording stub of package 07's `LandChange`, `OpenApproval` and `OnApprovalAnswered`
check.pseudocode: in internal/health/revert_test.go, a table over {the repair ended with 'session failed twice' -> requests [revert 7], entry '… (session failed twice); reverting change 7'; the repair ended with 'review disagreement' -> [revert 7]; the repair item landed as R and health exits 2 on R -> [revert 9, then revert 7 only after LandChange answered 'landed' for the reverting change of 9], entry '… (health command exited 2); reverting change 9 and change 7'}: drive svc.VerifyStep of item 12 and of the repair item until both return; assert the fake hub's revert requests in order; assert count(entries of kind 'revert') == 1 and unread; one more row: the fake hub already holds reverting change 10 of change 7 -> assert the incident uses change 10 and one revert request was sent

criteria.condition: the hub answers a revert with the reverting change, or names it in `409 already_reverted`
criteria.action: report the checks `nightshift-gate`, `nightshift-review` and `nightshift-release` as `passed` on the reverting change's version with the hub client's `ReportCheck`, each with the summary `revert after failed health command on <the landed commit of the item whose landing failed>`, and then ask `land.Service.LandChange(ctx, Request{Workspace, Change, Version})` of package 07 to land that version
criteria.contract: three reports with the reverting change's number, its version, the status `passed` and that summary reach the hub before the land is asked; the land request names that change and version; the summary of the repair's reverting change names the same commit; an outcome `landed` stores `LandedSHA` with the incident; an error of `LandChange` (the hub could not be asked) is returned from the step and the land is asked again at its next call

check.pseudocode: in internal/health/revert_test.go: the case 'the repair item landed and health fails' of the table above; assert the fake hub's checks of change 10 == {nightshift-gate, nightshift-review, nightshift-release} each 'passed' on version 1 with the summary 'revert after failed health command on ' + C; assert each report precedes lander.calls' LandChange({Workspace: 'demo', Change: 10, Version: 1}); the same for the reverting change of 7 with the same summary; LandChange returns an error once -> the step returns it, and the next call asks the same land and reports no check twice

criteria.condition: package 07's `LandChange` answers the land of a reverting change with the kind `pending_approval`
criteria.action: open an `approval` decision for the reverting change with `land.Service.OpenApproval(ctx, ApprovalRequest{Item, Workspace, Change, Version, Requirements, Owner: "revert"})`, mark it urgent with the inbox's `SetUrgent` (new in package 03's `internal/inbox`, added by this package), so that `GET /api/v1/decisions` lists it before every open decision that is not urgent, and ask for the same land again when the function registered with `OnApprovalAnswered("revert", fn)` is called with the option `approve`
criteria.contract: one `approval` decision on the thread of the item whose landing failed, answered with `urgent: true`; the open decisions are listed with the urgent ones first, oldest first among themselves, then the others oldest first; a decision opened through the inbox's `Open` with `Urgent: true` is urgent too, and one opened without it answers `urgent: false`; after `approve` the next call of the step asks `LandChange` with the same change and version and opens no second decision; `reject` and `abandon` are a refused land (REQ-3.5); the workspace stays `red` meanwhile

check.pseudocode: in internal/health/revert_test.go: lander.LandChange answers {Kind: 'pending_approval', Requirements: [rule nightshift-1]} and then 'landed'; svc.VerifyStep(ctx, item12); assert lander.calls hold OpenApproval({Item: 12, Workspace: 'demo', Change: 10, Version: 1, Requirements, Owner: 'revert'}); assert the decision is urgent; svc.VerifyStep again while it is open -> no second OpenApproval and no LandChange; call the registered fn with {Change: 10, Option: 'approve'}; svc.VerifyStep; assert LandChange was asked again for change 10. In internal/inbox/decision_test.go and internal/inbox/routes_test.go (package 03's files): open decisions A at T1, B at T2, C at T3 with Urgent true, D at T4 then inbox.SetUrgent(ctx, D, true); assert get('/api/v1/decisions') ids == [C, D, A, B] and items[0].urgent == true and items[2].urgent == false; answer C; assert ids == [D, A, B]; in internal/cli/inbox_test.go assert the Action section prints the served order

criteria.condition: every reverting change of an incident has landed and the health command exits 0 within the health timeout on the commit the last one landed as
criteria.action: set the workspace's state to `green`, append the entries `health` and `workspace_green` to the item's thread, move a repair item that is `verifying` to `awaiting_approval` and abandon it with the item service's `Abandon`, call `plan.Service.Reopen(ctx, item, "reverted after failed health command", extra)` of package 05, which moves the item to `awaiting_approval` and has its `plan` decision opened, with the evidence `health command output` (the output of the health command that failed on the item's landed commit) and `failed on` (that commit), and close the incident
criteria.contract: the workspace's state is `green`; the item is `awaiting_approval`; `Reopen` was called once with the item, the reason and the two pieces of evidence; the repair item is `abandoned`; the incident's phase is `closed`; a `Reopen` that returns another error than `plan.ErrNotFound` leaves the incident open and is asked again at the step's next call; for `plan.ErrNotFound` (an imported package, of which package 05 keeps no text) this package moves the item to `awaiting_approval` itself with that reason and appends an unread entry of the kind `revert` with the text `item <N> was reverted; its package was imported and has no plan to approve again: abandon it and import a corrected package`

check.pseudocode: in internal/health/revert_test.go: continue the case 'the repair item landed and health fails' with LandChange answering 'landed' as V for the last reverting change and stub.RunHealth for V returning {ExitCode: 0}; assert the health call == ('demo', V, 200); assert stub.state('demo') == 'green'; assert planner.calls == [Reopen(12, 'reverted after failed health command', [{Label: 'health command output', Text: the first tail}, {Label: 'failed on', Text: C}])]; assert items.Get(r).State == 'abandoned'; assert svc.Incident('demo') is none. Second case: Reopen fails once with a hub error -> the incident is not closed, and the next VerifyStep calls Reopen again and closes it. Third case: Reopen returns plan.ErrNotFound -> items.Get(12).State == 'awaiting_approval', the thread's last entry is of the kind 'revert' with the text above and unread, the incident is closed

criteria.condition: the health command exits with a code other than 0 or times out on the commit the last reverting change landed as, the hub refuses a revert with any answer other than `already_reverted`, `LandChange` answers the land of a reverting change with a kind other than `landed` and `pending_approval`, or the `approval` decision of a reverting change is answered `reject` or `abandon`
criteria.action: leave the workspace `red` and the item `verifying`, move the incident to the phase `main_red`, and open one decision of the kind `main_red` on the item's thread, with the evidence `health command output` (the last output) and `commits tried` (every commit of the incident a health command ran on, with its result, and every refusal), whose only option is `resume`
criteria.contract: the decision's `options` are exactly [`resume`], recommended, with `blocks` `workspace <slug>` and the question `Main branch of <slug> is unhealthy; resume when it is repaired?`; the workspace's state is `red`; no further repair, revert or land is asked while the decision is open; a second call of the step opens no second `main_red` decision

check.pseudocode: new file internal/health/mainred_test.go, a table over {health exits 1 on the revert's commit V, the fake hub answers the revert of 7 with 409 revert_conflict, the fake hub answers it 400 nothing_to_land, LandChange answers {Kind: 'blocked'} for the reverting change, LandChange answers {Kind: 'failed', Reason: 'land_failed: contention'}, the approval's fn is called with Option 'reject'}: drive svc.VerifyStep; d = the open decisions of item 12's thread; assert len(d) == 1 and d[0].kind == 'main_red' and keys(d[0].options) == ['resume']; assert its evidence 'commits tried' names C and, per row, V with its exit code or the refusal; assert stub.state('demo') == 'red'; assert items.Get(12).State == 'verifying'; call VerifyStep again; assert still one decision and no new hub request

requirements.title: Publishing to origin
requirements.rationale: The hub's branch is not where the project lives: work is done when origin has it, and origin must only ever get a branch the health command passed on.

criteria.condition: the scheduler calls the step of an item in `publishing` whose workspace is `green`, with no item of the workspace in `verifying` and no health run on a fast-forwarded tip pending, and the hub answers `POST …/branches/{default branch}/push` with the result `pushed` or `up_to_date`
criteria.action: append the entry `push` to the item's thread, move the item to `done`, and append the entry `published` with the text `change <n> is on origin as <commit>; <N> tokens spent`, marking the thread unread, where the commit is the change's landed commit and N the sum of the input, cache-creation and output tokens of every session of the item
criteria.contract: one push request, with the worker token and no `force`; the item is `done`; the thread is unread and holds `push of <branch> to origin: <result>` and the `published` entry; the hub saw no request that deletes, extends or otherwise changes the item's fork

setup: a publish service over a copy of the store template with the real item service, inbox and session table, the fake hub extended with a scriptable push route and an origin head per workspace, item 12 in `publishing` with change 7 landed as C and two sessions of 1,200 and 300 counted tokens
check.pseudocode: new file internal/publish/push_test.go, fixtures in internal/publish/helpers_test.go, a table over the fake hub's push result {'pushed', 'up_to_date'}: err = svc.PublishStep(ctx, item12); assert err == nil; assert the fake hub's push requests == [('demo', 'main', no force)]; assert items.Get(12).State == 'done'; assert entries hold {kind: 'push', text: 'push of main to origin: ' + result} and {kind: 'published', text: 'change 7 is on origin as ' + C + '; 1500 tokens spent'}; assert the thread is unread; assert the fake hub saw no request for the fork 'demo--i12'

criteria.condition: the hub answers the push with `409 non_fast_forward`
criteria.action: sync the workspace from origin once through `land.Service.SyncOrigin` of package 07, handle the default branch's result as REQ-5 says, and, where that lets work go on, ask the push once more in the same call of the step
criteria.contract: the hub sees a push, a sync and at most one more push in that order; a second `non_fast_forward` leaves the item `publishing` and the workspace `green`, opens no decision and is not counted as a failure; the next call of the step starts again with a push

check.pseudocode: in internal/publish/push_test.go, a table over {push 409 non_fast_forward, sync 'up_to_date', push 'pushed' -> item done and requests [push, sync, push]; push 409, sync 'ahead', push 409 again -> item 'publishing', workspace 'green', no decision, requests [push, sync, push]; push 409, sync 'diverged' -> requests [push, sync], workspace 'held' as REQ-5.4 says}: svc.PublishStep(ctx, item12); assert the fake hub's request log and the states

criteria.condition: the hub answers the push with `422 origin_rejected`, `502 origin_unauthenticated`, `502 origin_forbidden`, `502 origin_not_found`, or with any error answer other than `non_fast_forward`, `origin_unreachable`, `upstream_error` and `origin_timeout`
criteria.action: set the workspace's state to `held`, call `Notify` with the event `workspace_held`, open a decision of the kind `origin` on the thread of the item whose push it was, with the hub's error type and message as the reason, whose only option is `retry`, and leave the item `publishing`
criteria.contract: the workspace's state is `held`; the decision's `options` are exactly [`retry`], recommended, its question is `Origin refused the push of <branch> of <slug>: <message>; retry?`, its evidence `reason` holds `<error_type>: <message>` and `blocks` is `workspace <slug>`; one notification with `event: workspace_held`, the workspace, the item and the thread's path; the item is `publishing`; where the workspace has an open `origin` decision already, no second one is opened

check.pseudocode: in internal/publish/push_test.go, a table over the fake hub's push answers {422 origin_rejected 'protected branch hook declined', 502 origin_unauthenticated, 502 origin_forbidden, 502 origin_not_found, 404 branch_not_found}: svc.PublishStep(ctx, item12); assert ws.state('demo') == 'held'; d = open decisions of item 12's thread; assert len(d) == 1 and d[0].kind == 'origin' and keys(d[0].options) == ['retry']; assert d[0].question holds the hub's message; assert notifier.events == [{Event: 'workspace_held', Workspace: 'demo', Item: 12, Thread: path}]; assert items.Get(12).State == 'publishing'; svc.PublishStep(ctx, item13 of the same workspace); assert no second decision and no further push request

criteria.condition: the hub answers the push with `502 origin_unreachable`, `502 upstream_error` or `504 origin_timeout`
criteria.action: ask the push again no earlier than 1 minute after that answer, at most 5 further times in a row for the workspace, and handle the sixth such answer in a row as a refused push with its error type and message
criteria.contract: between two tries no push request is sent for the workspace, however often a step is called; the count is kept in the store, survives a restart and starts again at any other answer of the push; after the sixth answer in a row the workspace is `held` and an `origin` decision is open as REQ-4.3 says; until then the workspace stays `green`, the item `publishing` and no decision is opened

setup: an injected clock; the interval and the number of tries are parameters with the defaults 1 minute and 5
check.pseudocode: in internal/publish/push_test.go: the fake hub answers every push 504 origin_timeout; PublishStep at T0; assert 1 push request; PublishStep at T0+10s and T0+59s; assert still 1; advance to T0+60s; PublishStep; assert 2; repeat a minute apart until 6 requests; assert ws.state('demo') == 'held' and one 'origin' decision whose evidence 'reason' starts with 'origin_timeout'; second case: after 3 such answers reopen the store, answer the 4th push 'pushed'; assert the item is 'done' and the stored count is 0; assert the default interval is 1 minute and the default number of tries 5

criteria.condition: a workspace is `red` or `held`, an item of it is `verifying`, a health run on a fast-forwarded tip of it is pending, or the hub is not available to the worker token
criteria.action: send no push request for any item of that workspace, count no failure, and leave its `publishing` items `publishing`
criteria.contract: the step of a `publishing` item returns nil without a request to the hub's push route; the item's state and thread are unchanged; the first call after the condition ended sends the push

execution_paths.title: Origin refuses a push, and the person retries

steps.action: asks the hub to push the default branch of `demo` for item 14, which is `publishing`
refuses the update by a branch rule
answers `422 origin_rejected` with origin's reason
sets the workspace `held`, runs the notification command with `workspace_held` and opens an `origin` decision on the item's thread
reads the reason with `nightshift decision show <id>`, lifts the branch rule on the forge and runs `nightshift decide <id> --option retry`
sends the answer to `POST /api/v1/decisions/<id>/answer`
syncs the workspace, reads `ahead`, pushes, reads `pushed`, sets the workspace `green`, and at the item's next step moves it to `done`

symbols.name: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/revert
symbols.signature: scope changes:write; the owner of {slug}; optional body {title, intent, draft, auto_land, session_id}; 201 with the new change {number, version, state, reverts, …}, opened from the branch revert/<number> into the original's target; 409 change_not_landed; 409 already_reverted with error.details.reverted_by; 400 nothing_to_land; 409 revert_conflict with error.details.conflict; 400 target_not_found; a refusal leaves no branch and no change

symbols.name: GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}
symbols.signature: scope changes:read; 200 the change {number, state: draft|open|landed|abandoned, version, head_sha, landed: null | {sha, at, by, land_id, commits}, reverts, reverted_by, …}

symbols.name: PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/checks/{name}
symbols.signature: scope checks:write; body {status: pending|passed|failed, version, summary (at most 2,000 characters), url, details}; 200 with the check; one result per version and name, a report replaces the earlier one whole

symbols.name: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/land
symbols.signature: scope changes:write; optional body {expected_version, stack, override, session_id}; query wait 0..60; 200 the attempt with status landed and landed_sha; 202 still running; 409 land_conflict; 409 policy_blocked with blocked.status pending|blocked and blocked.requirements; 409 version_mismatch; 503 land_failed; the attempt in error.details

symbols.name: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/branches/{name}/push
symbols.signature: scope workspaces:write; optional body {force}; 200 {branch, sha, remote, remote_url, result: pushed|forced|up_to_date}; 409 non_fast_forward; 409 origin_moved (forced only); 422 origin_rejected (the message carries origin's reason); 502 origin_unauthenticated; 502 origin_forbidden, origin_not_found; 502 origin_unreachable, upstream_error; 504 origin_timeout; 404 branch_not_found; 400 fork_has_no_origin; 503 unavailable

symbols.name: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/sync
symbols.signature: scope workspaces:write; no body; 200 the workspace object plus branches: [{name, result: created|up_to_date|fast_forward|ahead|diverged|reset|name_conflict, local_sha (the hub's head after the sync), origin_sha}]; 400 fork_has_no_origin; 400 sync_disabled; 502 upstream_error; 500 internal

symbols.name: GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}
symbols.signature: 200 the workspace object with default_branch and head_sha, the hub's head of the default branch
